title: One claimable queue holds the work a run deferred, with enough payload for an absent agent
action: Build the one claimable queue D5 asks for: deferred capture, scribing, review, and promote-proposal work as REAL records an agent that was absent when they were queued can pick up and execute. New store, event-sourced JSONL, following the pattern backlog.rs already proves rather than inventing one. Record shape: an id, a `kind` (`capture` | `scribe` | `review` | `promote`), and a payload complete enough to act on with no session memory — feature, cells, areas, files, and a reason in the queuer's own words. Plus claim fields: owner, claimed_at, and a lease expiry. Reuse, do not reinvent: `lock::acquire_store_lock` for the store lock (its stale-takeover rule already handles a dead holder), `resolve_session_id`'s precedence chain for owner identity, backlog.rs's append-then-fold shape (pre-lock read-only fold and duplicate probe, acquire the lock, RE-fold under it as the race check, append, release), and the O_EXCL create protocol plus the dual-condition stale rule from cells/claims.rs — a claim is only reclaimable when the lease is expired AND the owner's heartbeat is stale, never on the lease alone. Verbs: add to the queue, list (filterable by kind and by claimed state), claim exactly one item (the point of the whole cell — two parallel agents must never get the same item), release, and complete. Every verb takes `--json`. The race is the risk, so prove it the way this repo proves races: real OS child processes contending for the same item, with an exact-count assertion that exactly one wins, plus a NEGATIVE CONTROL that must itself produce a violation when the claim is not exclusive, so the suite cannot pass vacuously. Search the repo for an existing multi-process race test and follow its shape. Do NOT migrate any existing store in this cell: `.bee/capture-queue.jsonl` and `.bee/review-candidates.jsonl` stay exactly as they are, and the derived scribing and promote scans stay too. This cell builds the queue; a later cell decides what feeds it. Verify the module wiring path yourself — the file list here is a guess at where a new verb module goes; if the crate wires verbs differently, follow the crate and record the corrected paths as a deviation.

truths: A queued item carries kind, feature, cells, areas, files, and a reason, and is executable with no session memory
Two concurrent OS processes claiming the same item produce exactly one winner, proven with an exact-count assertion
The race suite has a negative control that fails when exclusivity is removed, so it cannot pass vacuously
A claim is reclaimable only when the lease is expired AND the owner heartbeat is stale, never on expiry alone
list filters by kind and by claimed state, and every verb supports --json

It ran green in the run above. Note for the record: the control uses N threads behind a Barrier, not processes — that is this file's established falsifiability shape (:38) and the PROOF itself is multi-process, so the prohibition on an in-process test standing in for the multi-process proof is respected
